CERAKOTE vs Meguiar's Black Plastic Restorer: Which Restores Faded Trim Better?

Faded, chalky exterior trim is one of the fastest ways to make a car look older than it is. The CERAKOTE Ceramic Trim Coat Kit ($16.88) promises a semi-permanent ceramic coating for plastic trim, while Meguiar's Ultimate Black Plastic Restorer ($13.99) is the longtime go-to for quick restoration. We tested both to see which delivers the best results and the longest-lasting finish.

Published September 2026 · Based on verified Amazon product data

If you've got a car from the last 20 years, you've dealt with faded trim. The black plastic around windows, on the cowl, along rocker panels — it all turns gray and chalky under UV exposure. The difference between a $14 bottle of goop and a $17 ceramic coating can be night and day in terms of how long the results hold up.

CERAKOTE Ceramic Trim Coat Kit: $16.88, includes a 53ml ceramic coating bottle, two applicator blocks, six nitrile gloves, and a surface prep wipe. It's a true ceramic-based solution that cures to a hard, UV-resistant finish. The brand is best known for their firearms ceramic coatings, so they know a thing or two about durability.

Meguiar's Ultimate Black Plastic Restorer: $13.99, a 12 oz spray bottle of polymer-based trim dressing. Just spray on, wipe off, and walk away. It's the most popular trim restorer on Amazon with thousands of ratings. Meguiar's is the heavyweight champion of consumer car care products.

But here's the thing: one of these is a temporary dressing that washes off, and the other is a semi-permanent ceramic coating. They're fundamentally different products that happen to solve the same problem. Let's dig in.

Quick Verdict

Buy the CERAKOTE kit if: You want results that last months instead of weeks. The ceramic coating cures into a hard, hydrophobic layer that holds up through rain, car washes, and harsh sun. It's more work to apply (you need to prep carefully and let it cure for a few hours), but the results are dramatically better and longer-lasting. This is the right choice if you care about your car and don't want to reapply trim restorer every other wash.

Buy Meguiar's if: You want a quick, easy fix that looks great for a few weeks. Meguiar's Ultimate Black is perfect for a one-day detailing session, a car show, or selling your car. It's forgiving to apply, doesn't require prep work, and you can use it on interior trim too. But it won't last through more than a couple of car washes.

Our Pick: The CERAKOTE Ceramic Trim Coat Kit is the better product for anyone who wants lasting results. Yes, it takes more effort to apply, but one application lasts 6-12 months versus Meguiar's 2-4 weeks. Over a year, you'll save time and money with CERAKOTE.

Meguiar's Ultimate Black Plastic Restorer has been the go-to trim restorer for weekend detailers for years — and for good reason. The 12 oz spray bottle is easy to use: spray onto the trim, spread with a microfiber cloth, let it sit for a minute, and buff off any excess. That's it. No special applicators, no cure time, no gloves required.

The formula is a polymer-based dressing that restores color to faded trim and leaves a natural satin finish. It works on exterior trim (bumpers, side mirrors, window surrounds) as well as interior plastic, vinyl, and rubber. Meguiar's also includes UV blockers that help slow down future fading.

Where Meguiar's falls short is longevity. The product is a surface dressing, not a permanent coating. It will look fantastic for about 2-4 weeks, then gradually fade as rain, car washes, and UV exposure break it down. A single bottle typically lasts 5-8 applications on a mid-size car, so you'll go through 3-4 bottles per year if you want consistent results.

What's included: 12 oz spray bottle of Ultimate Black Plastic Restorer. Coverage: approximately 2-3 full applications on a sedan, depending on trim amount.

Real-World Performance: What Actually Matters

Longevity — The Biggest Difference

This is the deciding factor for most people. Meguiar's Ultimate Black looks great for about two weeks, then gradually loses its effect. You'll see it degrade fastest on horizontal surfaces (hood cowl, roof trim) that take direct sun and rain. Vertical trim pieces like door pillar appliqués will hold it a bit longer, maybe 3-4 weeks.

CERAKOTE, by contrast, is still going strong at the 3-month mark. Users report 6-12 months of consistent performance before they feel the need to reapply. The ceramic coating forms a physical barrier that doesn't wash off. If you park outside in a sunny climate, you'll see fading at the 8-10 month mark. Garage-kept cars can push a full year.

Ease of Application — Meguiar's Wins Here

Meguiar's is dead simple. Spray, wipe, done. You can do a whole car in 15 minutes. No prep work, no waiting. You don't even need to wash the car first, though you'll get better results if you do.

CERAKOTE requires more effort. You need to thoroughly clean and degrease the trim, apply the ceramic coating with the block applicator in thin coats, and then let it cure for several hours. The upside: you do the work once and don't think about it again for a year. The downside: if you don't prep properly, the coating won't bond well and you'll get uneven results.

Appearance — Both Look Great, Different Look

Meguiar's leaves a natural satin finish that most people describe as "factory new." It deepens the color of the plastic without looking wet or greasy. It's a very attractive, OEM-like appearance.

CERAKOTE has a slightly deeper, richer black finish that looks more like new plastic than restored plastic. The hydrophobic effect means water beads up dramatically — this is both functional and visually satisfying. The finish is slightly more "coated" looking than Meguiar's, but in a premium way rather than a plasticky way.

Pro Tip: For the best CERAKOTE results, use their included surface prep wipe followed by an isopropyl alcohol wipe (70% IPA) to remove any remaining oils. Apply the ceramic coating in thin, even coats — thicker is not better with ceramic coatings. Two thin layers with 30 minutes between them will outlast one thick layer.

Our Recommendation

Here's how we break it down:

Choose CERAKOTE Ceramic Trim Coat if: You plan to keep your car for more than a year. You don't mind spending 45 minutes on prep and application. You want a set-it-and-forget-it solution that looks great through all four seasons. The value proposition is clear — one $17 bottle outperforms four $14 bottles over a year, and you'll never have to look at faded trim between applications.

Choose Meguiar's Ultimate Black if: You want a quick fix for a car you're selling, or you prefer the ritual of a weekly detailing session. You want a product that works on interior trim too. You don't want to worry about curing times or application techniques. Meguiar's is the right tool for quick results and low commitment.

But honestly, for most people: Get the CERAKOTE kit. The extra $3 and one-time effort are worth it for results that last 10-20x longer. Frequently Asked Questions

Can I use CERAKOTE on headlight lenses?

No. CERAKOTE Ceramic Trim Coat is formulated specifically for textured plastic trim. Applying it to polycarbonate headlight lenses will cause hazing and poor optical clarity. For headlights, use a dedicated headlight restoration kit.

Will Meguiar's Ultimate Black damage my trim?

No, it's completely safe for all exterior automotive plastics, vinyl, and rubber. However, avoid getting it on painted surfaces as it can be difficult to remove if it dries. Wipe off any overspray immediately.

How long do I need to wait before washing the car after CERAKOTE application?

You should wait at least 24 hours before washing the car. The coating needs time to fully cure and cross-link. Rain is fine after 4-6 hours if the coating isn't touched, but avoid car washes, rain-x, or any physical contact with the treated surfaces for the first day.

Can I apply CERAKOTE over Meguiar's Ultimate Black?

Not recommended. The Meguiar's dressing sits on the surface and will prevent the ceramic coating from bonding. If you want to switch from Meguiar's to CERAKOTE, thoroughly clean the trim with a degreaser or isopropyl alcohol first to remove all traces of the previous dressing.

Does Meguiar's Ultimate Black work on interior dashboards?

Yes — and it's actually excellent for interior use. It leaves a natural, non-greasy finish that doesn't glare in sunlight. Use it on door panels, dashboards, center consoles, and even vinyl seats. Just don't use it on pedals, steering wheels, or shift knobs — it can be slippery.
